annotations.title: See what changes across the laws

description: What changes in Japanese law between two days, across every law japanlaw.org holds — 来年施行される改正、4月1日に変わる法令 — or one law's, or one topic's. Each change: the day it takes effect (day: on that day; by, a day a Cabinet Order sets, that day at the latest; open, not set yet), whether it is still to come, the law, the amending Act (titles, law number), its version, and its url. With no until, every change still to come is listed, those with no day yet last; since defaults to today. A long list stops at limit; continued.cursor, passed back as cursor with the same arguments, goes on. For what one change does, provision by provision, call get_amendments with its law and version. Link each change by its url.

cursor.description: Go on from here: the cursor an earlier answer's continued gave, with the same since, until, law and topic.

lang.description: The language of the pages every url opens, and of the card get_provision is drawn as: "en" (default) or "ja". The text returned always holds both languages.

law.description: One law's changes only: its Japanese title (労働基準法), English title, short name (労基法), slug or e-Gov law ID. Unset: every law's.

since.description: The first day, YYYY-MM-DD (2027-04-01). Unset: today.

topic.description: Only the changes of one topic's laws: work, immigration, tax, social-security, business, consumers, civil, housing, crime, transport or government.

until.description: The last day, YYYY-MM-DD. Unset: every change still to come, however far off, and those whose day is not set yet.
